subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Nyquist Criterion: Encirclement and Stability
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nyquist Criterion: Encirclement and Stability.

hook.text: The Nyquist plot traces the open-loop transfer function in the complex plane as frequency sweeps.

buildup.text: The Nyquist stability criterion counts how many times the plot encircles the critical point (-1, 0).

discovery.text: Zero encirclements mean stability for a system with no open-loop right-half-plane poles.

twist.text: Time delay adds phase lag that spirals the plot — making instability more likely at high frequencies.

climax.text: The Nyquist criterion handles cases Bode plots struggle with, like non-minimum-phase systems.

punchline.text: Count encirclements of minus one — Nyquist answers definitively.

quiz.question: In the Nyquist stability criterion, what point must not be encircled for a stable system?
